correctness.rationale: The proof combines two elementary valuation bounds with Jacobsthal scaling. A complementary-carry lemma gives nu_p(C(2k,k))+nu_p(C(2(N-k),N-k)) >= (r-nu_p(k))_+, while the shifted factor contributes the same deficit multiplied by A. For p-divisible indices the summand scales by a p-adic unit congruent to 1 modulo p^(3 min(r,nu_p(k))). Splitting into p-divisible and nondivisible indices yields the claimed exponent min(A+1,3)r. Endpoints, indices with nu_p(k)>r, and p-divisible m are handled explicitly. Exact finite checks support the proof.

originality.rationale: OEIS A364111, last modified in September 2026, still states the full A>=2,B,C>0 cubic supercongruence as a conjecture. Osburn-Sahu (2013) proves the analogous generalized Domb family with binom(n,k)^A, and Osburn-Sahu-Straub (2016) treats related Jacobsthal-scaled families, but the shifted family was not located among their stated results. Exact-formula, negative-upper-index, synonym, and identifier searches did not locate prior coverage. Coster's 1988 thesis was not fully inspected and remains a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: The cubic layer resolves an explicit generalized conjecture rather than a single parameter case. The same mechanism yields a sharp uniform hierarchy p^r, p^(2r), p^(3r) for A=0,1,>=2, with explicit examples attaining each exponent. The complementary central-binomial carry lemma is a reusable structural mechanism.
